subject.title: [Feature]: Add per-channel identity override for Discord bindings

question: Should ordinary Discord routed replies support a per-binding or per-agent visible identity override, and should that be implemented through webhook persona delivery, bot self-profile mutation, or deferred?
rationale: The request creates a new bot-credential-backed public identity surface, and the literal nickname approach does not match per-channel Discord semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent config/API, authorization boundary, fallback behavior, or cross-channel semantics.

options.title: Approve webhook persona delivery
options.body: Add a Discord plugin-owned routed-reply identity path that reuses webhook username/avatar delivery with explicit credential storage, fallback behavior, docs, tests, and live proof.

options.title: Coordinate with self-profile
options.body: Treat nickname/avatar mutation as part of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/34004 and add routed reply identity only after self-only action gates and guild/channel semantics are approved.

options.title: Defer routed identity
options.body: Keep current bot-account replies and thread-bound webhook persona behavior, asking users to use multiple bot accounts or existing thread-bound flows for now.

recommendation.title: Approve webhook persona delivery
recommendation.body: Add a Discord plugin-owned routed-reply identity path that reuses webhook username/avatar delivery with explicit credential storage, fallback behavior, docs, tests, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the closest public binding-contract PR, and the unresolved question is whether that binding surface should gain identity semantics.
